# portfolio sections — catalog

<!-- Generated by `npm run index` from component headers. Do not edit by hand. -->

Pick by USE WHEN, then read only the chosen file. Follow ../DIRECTION.md exactly.

- **about-block.tsx** — The first-person bio — a big left margin, two or three confident sentences at reading-display size, a small offset portrait slot, recognitions as one quiet line.
- **clients-line.tsx** — Naming past clients without ceremony — one muted paragraph of names separated by middle dots under a small index label. The quiet alternative to a logo wall.
- **colophon.tsx** — The small end-of-page production note — typeface, toolkit, photo credits — one muted row over a thin rule, sitting between the last section and footer-line.
- **contact-cta.tsx** — The closing ask — one display-scale line, the email as a huge underlined link that inverts on hover, and a small location/timezone line. No form, no buttons.
- **experience-list.tsx** — A CV condensed to two short ledgers — "Experience" (role, place, years) beside "Teaching / Talks" (event, year) — closing with a mailto for the full CV.
- **footer-line.tsx** — The one-line sign-off — name, year, colophon note, and two or three text links over a thin top rule. Nothing else; the page has already said everything.
- **hero-statement.tsx** — The opening screen of a personal portfolio — a full viewport of type where the name or a one-line position statement IS the design. No imagery, no CTA buttons.
- **process-note.tsx** — A short working-note or manifesto — how the studio actually operates — set at reading-display size with a big left margin and one bold pull-line. No imagery.
- **project-feature.tsx** — One case study deserves the full stage — a near-full-bleed hero image, then a two-thirds summary paragraph beside a one-third factual metadata list.
- **recognitions-list.tsx** — Awards and press deserve their own quiet index — thin-ruled rows of year, award or publication, and the project it honored. Factual, no logos, no badges.
- **services-list.tsx** — Capabilities as a short numbered ledger — 01–04 rows, service name in bold, one factual line each. No cards, no icons, no pricing.
- **work-grid.tsx** — The body of work shown visually — an asymmetric two-column image grid with small factual captions. Alternative to work-index.tsx when the work photographs well.
- **work-index.tsx** — The main body of work as a printed-index list — name, client/category, year in thin-ruled rows. The right choice when the work is better named than pictured.
